subStages.title: Functional Requirements
subStages.prompt: What are the core functional requirements? List 3-5 'Users should be able to...' statements that capture the must-have behavior.

tip.label: Use 'Users should be able to...'
tip.description: Keep them as user actions, not implementation details.

subStages.title: Non-Functional Requirements
subStages.prompt: What are the non-functional requirements? Cover availability vs consistency, latency targets, scale (DAU/QPS), durability, and security where relevant.

tip.label: Quantify everything
tip.description: Latency, scale, availability — every NFR needs a number.

stages.title: Core Entities
stages.prompt: What are the core entities (the 'nouns') in this system? List them — schemas come later.

tip.label: Just a List
tip.description: Don't worry about schemas yet. Just the names of the nouns.

stages.title: API
stages.prompt: Define the API surface: endpoints, methods, request/response shapes. One row per functional requirement.

tip.label: Method + Path + Body
tip.description: One line per endpoint. REST is the default.

stages.title: Data Flow
stages.prompt: For data-processing systems only: describe the high-level sequence from input to output.

tip.label: Steps in order
tip.description: Number each step from input → output.

stages.title: High-Level Design
stages.prompt: Draw boxes and arrows for the major components. Walk through each API endpoint end-to-end. Note schema fields next to databases.

tip.label: Boxes and Arrows
tip.description: Walk through each API endpoint end-to-end.

stages.title: Deep Dives
stages.prompt: Harden the design against the non-functional requirements. Address scaling, bottlenecks, edge cases, failure modes.

tip.label: Address NFRs concretely
tip.description: Pick the riskiest two and walk through mechanisms.
